title: By Allah, I will deal with your idols once you leave.
subtitle: A resolve made openly, before the festival
then: Ibrahim swore an oath, {idea}which some of his people heard{/idea}, to break their idols after they went out to their festival. Ibn Mas'ud reported that when they passed him on the way and asked if he was coming, {trap}he said, I am sick{/trap}.
now: You have talked for months about clearing the haram subscriptions off your phone, or the habit you hate. {trap}Talk has become the whole plan.{/trap} {idea}Ibrahim set a time and followed through.{/idea}
new: Conviction becomes real when I decide when and how I will act.
try: Pick one bad habit and name the exact time today you will remove it.

title: He broke them all, but left the biggest standing.
subtitle: A question set up for the people to face
then: Ibrahim {trap}smashed all the idols except the biggest{/trap}. It was said he put the hammer in its hands, so people would wonder if it had broken the rest. The aim was {idea}that they might turn to it{/idea} and see for themselves.
now: Your friend insists a lucky charm or a horoscope app runs her week. You could mock it. {idea}A good question that lets her see it herself{/idea} often works better than a lecture.
old: To change someone's mind, I need to win the argument.
new: Sometimes the best move is to set up a question they answer themselves.
try: In one disagreement today, ask a sincere question instead of making a point.

title: Who did this to our gods? Gods who could not protect themselves.
subtitle: The scene that should have opened their eyes
then: They returned and saw what Ibrahim had done, {trap}humiliating their idols{/trap} and lowering their status. The tafsir says it was {idea}proof they were not divine{/idea}. Still, their first thought was to find and blame the one who did it.
now: Your plan built on that one investment collapses. Your first instinct is to find who to blame. {idea}The better question is why you trusted something that couldn't hold.{/idea}
old: When something I relied on fails, I look for who is at fault.
new: When something I relied on falls, I should ask why I relied on it.
try: Think of one thing that let you down recently. Ask what it shows about where your trust was.

title: We heard a young man named Ibrahim speak of them.
subtitle: One young voice remembered in a whole town
then: Those who had heard his oath said: {idea}we heard a young man talking about them, called Ibrahim{/idea}. He was alone against the whole town's religion. {reward}His words had been noticed{/reward} even before the idols fell.
now: You are the only one in the office who doesn't join the gossip, the only one in the friend group who prays. {trap}You feel invisible.{/trap} {reward}People notice more than you think.{/reward}
old: I'm one person. What I stand for goes unnoticed.
new: One young voice stood against a whole town. People notice what I stand for.
try: Do one small right thing today in front of others, without fuss.

title: Bring him before everyone, they said. That was his aim.
subtitle: Their trial became his stage
then: They wanted him {trap}brought before a large audience{/trap} as witnesses. The tafsir says {idea}this was Ibrahim's ultimate purpose{/idea}: to tell the whole gathering how foolish it was to worship idols that could not defend themselves.
now: You are called into the meeting to explain why you refused to sign off the false figures. It feels like being put on trial. {reward}It may also be the moment everyone hears why honesty matters.{/reward}
old: Being put on the spot is the worst thing that can happen.
new: The moment they put me on the spot can be the moment truth gets heard.
try: If you are challenged on something right today, answer calmly and clearly.

title: Was it you who did this to our gods, Ibrahim?
subtitle: The question at the centre of the gathering
then: Before everyone, they asked: {trap}are you the one who did this to our gods, O Ibrahim?{/trap} They thought he was on trial. {idea}In truth, their gods were{/idea}, broken and unable to say a word.
now: Your family questions why you stopped joining in a habit you all shared. {trap}You feel you are the one being judged.{/trap} {idea}Sometimes the question you are asked puts the old habit on trial instead.{/idea}
old: When I am questioned, I am the one on trial.
new: When I am questioned for doing right, the wrong is what is really on trial.
try: If someone questions your faith choices today, answer with one honest sentence, not defensively.

title: The big one did it. Ask them, if they can speak.
subtitle: A reply that made the idols answer for themselves
then: Ibrahim pointed to the idol he had left whole: {idea}ask them, if they can speak!{/idea} The tafsir says he hoped {reward}they would admit of their own will{/reward} that the idols could not speak, because they were lifeless.
now: You keep checking the stock app or the follower count as if it will tell you you're okay. {trap}Ask it anything that matters. It says nothing.{/trap} {idea}What cannot answer you cannot guide you.{/idea}
old: The things I check for reassurance tell me how I am doing.
new: What cannot speak, hear, or answer cannot be what I turn to.
try: Next time you reach for something for reassurance, make a short dua instead.

title: For a moment they turned on themselves: we are the wrongdoers.
subtitle: A flash of self-blame, aimed at the wrong thing
then: The tafsir explains they {trap}blamed themselves for not protecting their gods{/trap}: you are the wrongdoers because you neglected them. {idea}They came close to the point and missed it.{/idea} A god that needs guarding is no god.
now: The diet failed, so you blame yourself for not trying hard enough, then try the same fad again. {trap}You fix the details and keep the bad idea.{/trap} {idea}Sometimes the plan itself is what needs dropping.{/idea}
old: When something fails, I just need to try harder at it.
new: Sometimes the failure is not my effort but the thing I put my trust in.
try: Look at one repeated failure in your life and ask whether the goal itself is wrong.

title: Heads down, they admitted: you know these cannot speak.
subtitle: The truth spoken, and then turned away from
then: The tafsir says {trap}they looked at the ground{/trap}. Qatadah said they admitted their guilt and confusion: {idea}you know well these do not speak{/idea}, so how can you tell us to ask them? They had said the truth out loud.
now: You admit to your spouse that the phone at dinner is a problem. You both nod. {trap}Next evening, same thing.{/trap} {idea}Saying the truth is the first step, not the last.{/idea}
old: Admitting I'm wrong is the hard part, and I've done it.
new: Admitting the truth only helps if I let it change what I do.
try: Take one thing you have already admitted is wrong, and change one detail of it today.

title: Then why worship what cannot help you or harm you?
subtitle: Ibrahim draws the conclusion from their own words
then: Once they admitted it, Ibrahim said: if they cannot speak, {trap}and can neither benefit nor harm you{/trap}, {idea}why do you worship them instead of Allah?{/idea} He used their own answer to make the case.
now: You feel anxious if you miss your morning ritual of checking the news, or that good-luck routine before an interview. {trap}It neither helps nor hurts.{/trap} {idea}Your hope belongs with the One who actually can.{/idea}
old: Some of my habits keep things going well for me.
new: If something cannot help or harm me, it does not deserve my hope or fear.
try: Replace one superstitious habit today with Bismillah and a short dua.

title: Shame on you and your idols. Will you not think?
subtitle: The argument ends with a call to reason
then: Ibrahim asked if they did not realize {trap}the extent of the misguidance they were following{/trap}. The tafsir says {idea}he defeated them in argument and left them with no way out{/idea}. Allah calls it the proof He gave Ibrahim against his people.
now: You know the facts about your spending, your sleep, your screen time. {trap}You just never sit down and think them through.{/trap} {idea}Faith asks you to use the mind you were given.{/idea}
old: Thinking too hard about my life only makes me anxious.
new: Allah asks me to think. Clear thinking leads me back to Him.
try: Sit for five minutes today and honestly think through one habit and where it leads.

title: Out of arguments, they shouted: burn him, defend your gods.
subtitle: When reasoning fails, force takes over
then: When {trap}their arguments were refuted and falsehood defeated{/trap}, they turned to power and said: burn him. They gathered a huge amount of wood. Ibn 'Abbas reported that as Ibrahim was thrown, he said {reward}Allah is sufficient for me, and He is the best disposer of affairs{/reward}.
now: You make a fair point in the family argument and someone starts shouting or threatening. {trap}Volume rises when reasons run out.{/trap} {reward}Ibrahim's words fit that moment too: Allah is enough for me.{/reward}
old: When I am losing an argument, I need to push harder.
new: When I run out of reasons, I should stop, not get louder. Allah is enough.
try: When you feel cornered today, say Hasbiyallahu wa ni'mal wakil and lower your voice.

title: O fire, be cool and safe for Ibrahim.
subtitle: Allah's command over the thing meant to destroy
then: Ibn 'Abbas said the angel of rain asked when he would be told to send rain, but {idea}Allah's command was swifter{/idea}: O fire, be coolness and safety. Ibn 'Abbas and Abu Al-'Aliyah said that without the word {reward}safety{/reward}, Ibrahim would have been harmed by the cold.
now: The redundancy letter, the diagnosis, the court date. {trap}It looks like fire.{/trap} {idea}The same Lord who spoke to Ibrahim's fire is your Lord.{/idea} {reward}He can make the hard thing safe for you.{/reward}
old: Some situations are simply too dangerous to come through.
new: Nothing harms except by Allah's leave. He can make the fire safe.
try: Name the thing you fear most right now, and ask Allah to make it cool and safe for you.

title: They plotted to harm him, and became the greatest losers.
subtitle: A plot against a prophet turned on the plotters
then: They {trap}wanted to plot against the Prophet of Allah{/trap}, the tafsir says, {idea}but Allah planned against them and saved him from the fire{/idea}. They were defeated and humiliated. The whole town lost to one young man who relied on Allah.
now: Someone at work is quietly trying to get you pushed out. You are tempted to plot back. {idea}Stay honest, do your work, rely on Allah.{/idea} {reward}His plan outlasts theirs.{/reward}
old: If someone plots against me, I have to out-plot them.
new: Allah's plan outlasts every plot. My job is to stay upright and rely on Him.
try: Instead of planning a comeback against someone, make dua for your own protection and their guidance.
